title: Stress Tensor in Fundamental Measure Theory of Hard-Sphere Fluids: A Thermomechanical Approach
authors: Yury A. Budkov, Nikolai N. Kalikin
abstract: We derive the local pressure tensor generated by the original Rosenfeld fundamental measure theory (FMT) for hard-sphere fluids from an arbitrary infinitesimal deformation. The variation of a finite-distance FMT kernel is written via the line integrals of the local deformation gradient along the straight segment connecting its endpoints. The resulting symmetric pressure tensor consists of a local term expressed through the standard FMT weighted densities and a finite-range chord term. For a monodisperse hard-sphere fluid, differential relations between the Rosenfeld measures reduce the tensor to a closed one-body form. We demonstrate that no independent pair density or inhomogeneous Ornstein--Zernike equation is required. In the limit of homogeneous fluid the tensor reproduces the Percus--Yevick compressibility equation of state. In planar confinement the normal stress satisfies the hard-wall contact relation, the mechanical surface tension agrees with the surface excess grand potential, and the disjoining pressure agrees with the derivative of the confined grand potential with respect to slit width. The finite-range chord term extends the deformation method from local field theories to nonlocal weighted-density functionals.
summary: This work develops a rigorous thermomechanical framework to calculate the pressure tensor for hard-sphere fluids using Fundamental Measure Theory (FMT). By analyzing the free energy's response to infinitesimal deformations, the authors derive a closed-form expression for the stress tensor. This confirms the theory's consistency by matching known results for bulk fluids and confined geometries.
main_problem: The paper derives the local pressure tensor for hard-sphere fluids using the Rosenfeld Fundamental Measure Theory (FMT) by analyzing the system's response to infinitesimal spatial deformations.
main_result: The resulting pressure tensor is shown to be in a closed one-body form for monodisperse hard spheres, successfully reproducing known equations of state (like Percus-Yevick) and boundary conditions in various limits.
method: The core method is a thermomechanical approach, calculating the stress tensor from the variation of the excess free energy functional with respect to an infinitesimal deformation gradient.
model_or_system: The system studied is hard-sphere fluids, modeled using the Rosenfeld FMT, which provides a non-local description of the excess free energy functional.
key_observables: The symmetric pressure tensor (P_ij), normal stress, tangential stress, and disjoining pressure.
important_parameters: The fluid density ($ho$), the confinement width ($H$), and the deformation parameters ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the applicability of the thermomechanical route to nonlocal functionals and assumes the straight chord approximation for the deformation kernel.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail derivations involving stress tensor components (C_zz, C_xx) and the long-wavelength expansion of the FMT kernel.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the pressure tensor by first establishing the general deformation relation, then applying it to the FMT functional, and finally verifying the results in specific limits like bulk fluid, planar confinement, and analyzing stress anisotropy.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the rigorous derivation of stress tensors from free energy functionals using deformation methods is a foundational technique in statistical mechanics that underpins many modern theories of many-body systems.
